Brian Silverman's 4-state Moore-neighborhood CA that models electron flow in wires; Turing-complete (a full RISC computer was built in it) but has no heredity, agents, evolution, or physics. Verified: real, distinct computational CA; scores hold under rubric (no A-life properties, consc0, substrate1 correct).

Chris Langton's A-Life turmite: one agent on a grid, two rules, that self-organizes chaos into an emergent periodic 'highway'; single agent, no reproduction, mutation, or learning. Verified real/distinct; scores defensible (single-agent, no heredity/ecology/cognition).

Langton's 8-state 86-cell loop that copies its genetic instruction stream out an arm to spawn a daughter loop; landmark 'third-generation' self-replicator but blind copying with no mutation/selection or open-ended novelty. Verified real/distinct; repro4 defensible (real self-replication of an instruction stream, below Avida's mutation+selection 5), peer5 justified by foundational status.

The 29-state CA that first proved machine self-replication is logically possible via a tape-driven universal constructor+copier; foundational to all A-Life reproduction theory but abstract, no ecology/physics/rendering. Verified real/distinct; scores hold (repro4 for tape-driven self-reproduction, open2 slightly generous but within tolerance given universal-construction capacity, instr1/vis2 correct for a mostly-theoretical CA rarely fully simulated).

Wolfram's Class-4 elementary 1D CA with interacting localized gliders; proven Turing-complete by Cook (2004) via cyclic tag systems, but a pure computational CA with no agents, heredity, or embodiment. Verified real/distinct; all scores defensible (computational CA, no A-life axes, peer5 for landmark Turing-completeness result).

Rafler's continuous-domain generalization of Conway's Life (floating-point cells, disk-averaged neighborhoods) producing smooth self-propelling glider-like blobs; the direct precursor to Lenia, less adopted and no evolution/learning. Source verified (arXiv:1111.1567, Stephan Rafler, 'Generalization of Conway's Game of Life to a continuous domain - SmoothLife'). Scores defensible vs Lenia anchor (morph3/vis4 sit just below Lenia's 4/5).

Kellie Evans' large-neighborhood birth/death generalization of Life whose organic 'bugs' and gliders converge to a proven continuum limit (RealLife); rich morphology and a key Lenia ancestor but no heredity, learning, or ecology. Verified real/distinct (Evans' large-radius life-like CA, a documented Lenia precursor). Scores mirror SmoothLife and are defensible; source is Evans' continuum-limit paper.

type: automata chemistry / artificial chemistry OEE vehicle
basis: VERIFIED real (alife.org encyclopedia entry; Hickinbotham, Clark, Stepney et al., York). Molecules are opcode strings that bind by soft template matching (imperfect matches bind with lower probability); a bound string executes as a replicase and copies its partner with copy errors, so mutation+selection is the core engine (repro=5, Tierra-class). Documented replicator-parasite ecologies and hypercycles (eco=3, matching Tierra) plus an evolved von Neumann universal-constructor architecture ('semantic closure'); explicitly built as an open-ended-evolution vehicle with demonstrated variation+innovation+emergence, but no claim of indefinite novelty growth so open=4 (below Geb/ASAL 5). type: self-replicating loop CA with natural selection
basis: VERIFIED real (Sayama, 'A new structurally dissolvable self-reproducing loop evolving in a simple cellular automata space', Artificial Life 5(4):343-65, 1999; 25-year retrospective by Sayama & Nehaniv, arXiv:2402.03961, confirms it 'proved constructively that Darwinian evolution of self-reproducing organisms by variation and natural selection is possible within deterministic cellular automata'). Nine-state CA descendant of Langton's Loops whose loops dissolve structurally on collision, so phenotype interaction generates heritable variation with NO injected mutation operator: self-replication + variation + natural selection is the Avida/Tierra bar (repro=5, above Langton's Loops 4 whose copying is blind). Famously CONVERGENT, not open-ended: the 1999 abstract states smaller individuals are naturally selected for quicker self-reproduction and 'the whole population gradually evolved toward the smallest ones' (open=2). Single species competing only for space (eco=2, below Tierra 3). Pure CA: morph=0, cog=0, substrate=1; instr=2/vis=3 match the Langton's Loops anchor. consc=0.

VERIFIED real (Kriegman, Blackiston, Levin & Bongard, 'Kinematic self-replication in reconfigurable organisms', PNAS 118(49), 2021; preceded by the PNAS 2020 design-pipeline paper; project site krorgs.github.io). Frog stem cells assembled into motile organisms that replicate KINEMATICALLY by pushing loose cells into piles that mature into copies; an evolutionary search in voxel soft-body simulation found the semitoroidal 'Pac-Man' shape that sustains extra replication rounds. Real living bodies under real physics (morph=5, genuinely above this project's 3.8). repro=3: authentic self-replication but no genome, mutation, or heritable variation in the lineage, so it sits with Primordial Particle Systems (3) not Langton's Loops (4) - the selection ran in silico at design time, not in the organisms. Cells are skin/cardiac with NO neurons: cog=0. eco=2 (multiple parents pile a shared free-cell resource, no trophic web). substrate=1 per the GOLEM precedent (evolve-in-sim then realize physically is still one computational substrate). vis=3 matches GOLEM (sim renders plus physical artifact). consc=0.

VERIFIED real (Liu, Matthews, Kriegman & Bongard, 2020; github.com/voxcraft/voxcraft-sim, CUDA). GPU-parallel successor to the Voxelyze soft-body engine and the de-facto substrate under the xenobot design pipeline and the sim2real soft-robot transfer work; headless, emitting per-voxel history traces replayed by the separate voxcraft-viz tool, with evolution living in the separate voxcraft-evo - hence repro=1/open=1/cog=0, matching the Voxelyze anchor. NEAR-DUPLICATE of the Voxelyze / VoxCAD row (same engine lineage, distinguished as the CUDA reimplementation) - confidence lowered to 0.8 to reflect the overlap, per the UNIMAL/DERL precedent. instr=3 and peer=3 sit BELOW Voxelyze's 4/4: newer, thinner documentation, and no journal paper of its own. eco=0, substrate=1, consc=0.

VERIFIED real (Suarez, Du, Zhu, Mordatch & Isola, 'The Neural MMO Platform for Massively Multiagent Research', NeurIPS Datasets & Benchmarks 2021; originally OpenAI 2019; NeurIPS 2022/2023 competitions). Up to 128 concurrent agents forage food/water, fight in a rock-paper-scissors melee/ranged/magic triangle, level interdependent professions, loot scripted NPCs and trade on a global market - one of the richest agent ecologies in the survey (eco=4, above this project's 3.3). repro=0: agents SPAWN from a pool at one per tick up to the 128 cap and are RL-trained; there is no genome, descent, or heredity of any kind. open=3 not 5: worlds are procedural and the paper markets 'open-ended tasks', but the achievement/profession space is authored and fixed - agents do not generate new tasks (below POET/OMNI 5). 2D tile world, no physics (morph=1); cog=4 (PPO agents showing real skill progression); instr=4 (open source, logging/visualization tooling, competition infrastructure). substrate=1, consc=0.

VERIFIED real (Leibo, Duenez-Guzman, Vezhnevets, Agapiou, Sunehag, Koster, Matyas, Beattie, Mordatch & Graepel, 'Scalable Evaluation of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Melting Pot', ICML 2021; google-deepmind/meltingpot). DMLab2D gridworlds posing cooperation, competition, deception and reciprocation, scored by generalization to HELD-OUT social scenarios populated with unfamiliar co-players, plus a universalization test. instr=5 is the entire point of the system - 50+ substrates and 250+ held-out test scenarios in Melting Pot 2.0 - a stricter evaluation apparatus than this project's self-scored 4.4. eco=4 (dense social interdependence and commons dilemmas). Deliberately FIXED scenario set with no novelty generation (open=2) and no reproduction of any kind (repro=0). 2D sprites, no physics (morph=1/vis=3); cog=4 (RL agents with social strategy). substrate=1, consc=0.

VERIFIED real (Matthews, Beukman, Ellis, Samvelyan, Jackson, Coward & Foerster, 'Craftax: A Lightning-Fast Benchmark for Open-Ended Reinforcement Learning', ICML 2024 Spotlight; MichaelTMatthews/Craftax). VERIFIED real (Marius Buliga, IMAR; 'Artificial chemistry experiments with chemlambda, lambda calculus, interaction combinators', arXiv:2003.14332; also Buliga & Kauffman, 'Chemlambda, universality and self-multiplication'). Molecules are graphs over 9 node types rewritten by enzyme-like local rules; a 'quine graph' reproduces itself under a maximal set of non-conflicting rewrites, and under a RANDOM rewriting algorithm quines exhibit metabolism, multiply, or die. repro=3: real structural self-multiplication but NO documented mutation, heritable variation, or selection, so it sits with Primordial Particle Systems (3) and below the blind-but-canonical Langton's Loops (4). Aspatial graphs (morph=0), no agents or learning (cog=0/eco=1), no OEE claims (open=2). vis=3 for the 200+ published animations and live JS demos. peer=2 per the Clusters precedent: real arXiv publications but essentially a single-author project with minimal adoption. Evolutionary claims were hard to pin down from sources: confidence 0.7. Era given as 2010s because an exact origin year could not be verified. substrate=1, consc=0.

Kinetic steering only, no bodies or collision (morph=2, between Boids 1 and PPS 3) and no learning (cog=0, matching Boids). vis=4, instr=3, peer=3 (Artificial Life journal, prominent author, multiple follow-ups, niche adoption). substrate=1, consc=0.

VERIFIED real (Varela, Maturana & Uribe, 'Autopoiesis: the organization of living systems, its characterization and a model', BioSystems 5:187-196, 1974, aka PROTOBIO; source_url is McMullin's 'Thirty years of computational autopoiesis: a review', Artificial Life 10(3):277-95, 2004 - the canonical account, verified, which confirms the model as seminal 'over a decade in advance of the first Santa Fe Workshop on Artificial Life' and notes the programme 'sharply illuminated both conceptual and methodological problems'). Substrate particles diffuse on a 2D tessellation, a catalyst concatenates them into links, and links close into a membrane that self-repairs by replacing decayed components. repro=1 is the hostile-but-correct read: the founding model of 'the organization of the living' only SELF-MAINTAINS - it yields no offspring and never divides - so it scores at Gray-Scott's level despite its stature. No evolution (open=1), no learning (cog=0), one cell in a soup (eco=1). instr=1 matches the von Neumann constructor: figures were hand-drawn from FORTRAN output and the published algorithm proved ambiguous enough that reimplementation became its own literature. morph=2 (2D spatial chemistry, below Squirm3's 3). peer=4 for foundational status. consc=0: autopoiesis-as-cognition is a LATER extension (Maturana & Varela 1980) and is not in this model.

VERIFIED real (Stan Franklin et al., Cognitive Computing Research Group, University of Memphis; 'LIDA: A computational model of global workspace theory and developmental learning', AAAI 2007; 'Consciousness is computational: The LIDA model of global workspace theory', Int. J. Machine Consciousness 1(1), 2009; successor to the Navy-funded IDA agent). Attention codelets form coalitions that COMPETE for a global workspace whose winner is broadcast to all modules on a ~10 Hz cognitive cycle (understand -> consciousness -> action selection), over sensory, perceptual-associative, episodic, declarative and procedural memory. consc=5: this is the canonical computational implementation of Baars' Global Workspace Theory and it legitimately BEATS this project's self-scored 3.5 on the consciousness-theory axis. cog=4 not 5: several learning modes are specified but thinly demonstrated versus the deep-RL controllers at 5. Software agents in toy domains, no physics (morph=1, matching Geb), no world rendering (vis=1), no reproduction or novelty generation (repro=0/open=1/eco=1). peer=3.5: heavily cited in machine consciousness, but adoption outside the Memphis group is thin and the architecture is more specified than validated. Era 2000s (LIDA proper dates from ~2006, extending the earlier IDA). substrate=1.

VERIFIED real (Fontana & Buss, 'The arrival of the fittest: Toward a theory of biological organization', Bulletin of Mathematical Biology 56(1), 1994; source_url is Mathis, Patel, Weimer & Forrest, 'Self-Organization in Computation & Chemistry: Return to AlChemy', Chaos 34(9), 2024, which reproduced the original with modern compute and found 'a surprising mix of dynamical robustness and fragility'). Lambda expressions collide in a well-mixed reactor and function application IS the reaction, spontaneously yielding selfish replicators, then self-maintaining autocatalytic organizations, then mutually-dependent ecosystems (eco=3). repro=3: self-replication genuinely EMERGES from a random soup, but Fontana & Buss deliberately included no fitness function and no mutation operator - the whole point was the arrival of the fittest rather than the survival of it - so it sits with Primordial Particle Systems (3), below Amoeba (4) which adds competition for memory/CPU. open=3: real emergent organizational novelty that nonetheless settles into stable levels. Aspatial (morph=0), no agents or learning (cog=0), no rendering (vis=1). instr=3 (independent reimplementations including LambdaReactor, plus the 2024 replication). peer=4 (foundational artificial chemistry). substrate=1, consc=0.

VERIFIED real (Lenore Blum & Manuel Blum, 'A theory of consciousness from a theoretical computer science perspective: Insights from the Conscious Turing Machine', PNAS 119(21), 2022; arXiv:2107.13704). A formal TCS machine in which long-term-memory processors compete via a chunk-scoring tournament for a tiny short-term memory whose contents are broadcast back to every processor - offered as a substrate-independent formalization of Baars/Dehaene Global Workspace Theory, and used to account for blindsight, inattentional blindness, change blindness, dreaming and free will. consc=5: an explicit, peer-reviewed formal theory of consciousness, above this project's self-scored 3.5. Everything else is near-zero BY CONSTRUCTION - it is mathematics, not a running world: no reproduction, ecology, bodies or rendering (repro/open/eco/morph/vis=0); instr=1 matches the von Neumann constructor as the survey's other purely-theoretical entry. cog=3 (a specified cognitive model, largely unimplemented). peer=3: PNAS and a Turing-Award author, but contested in the literature (see the critique 'Evaluating the explanatory power of the Conscious Turing Machine') and adopted as a running platform by nobody. SCOPE NOTE: a theory entry rather than an A-Life world, included on the same basis as the von Neumann constructor and as an honest anchor for the otherwise near-empty consciousness axis. substrate=1.

VERIFIED real (Ghaffarizadeh, Heiland, Friedman, Mumenthaler & Macklin, 'PhysiCell: An open source physics-based cell simulator for 3-D multicellular systems', PLOS Computational Biology, 2018; MathCancer/PhysiCell). Off-lattice cell agents with force-based adhesion/repulsion/motility, fluid-and-solid volume regulation and cycle/apoptosis/necrosis models, coupled to the BioFVM solver for reaction-diffusion PDEs with cell-centered and bulk sources/sinks; 10^5-10^6 cells on a workstation. substrate=2 is earned honestly - cell-agent mechanics AND a reaction-diffusion PDE field are two genuinely distinct coupled substrates (the DevoWorm level, still far below this project's 4.6). instr=5: PLOS venue, MultiCellDS standardized output, PhysiCell Studio, and heavy cancer/immuno adoption - above this project's 4.4. repro=2: mitosis with phenotype inheritance IS in the standard library and the published heterogeneity example shows real clonal selection on an 'oncoprotein' trait, but there is no genome or mutation operator in the core, so it sits above NetLogo-class optional heredity (1) and below genuine mutation+selection (4). eco=3 (cells compete for diffusing oxygen/nutrients and secrete signals). morph=4 (real cell mechanics, below Voxelyze/OpenWorm soft-body 5). cog=0, open=1, consc=0.

type: 2D mass-spring creature construction and race domain
basis: VERIFIED real (Ed Burton / Soda, launched April 2000; won an Interactive Arts BAFTA in 2001; Sodarace ran as a human-versus-machine 'online olympics' with Queen Mary University of London). type: evolved-controller artificial ant (GA over FSA and ANN)
basis: VERIFIED real (Jefferson, Collins, Cooper, Dyer, Flowers, Korf, Taylor & Wang, 'The Genesys System: Evolution as a Theme in Artificial Life', Artificial Life II, 1991; full paper live at the source_url). A GA on a Connection Machine evolves ants to follow the crooked, broken John Muir trail on a 32x32 toroidal grid within 200 steps, using either 32-state finite-state automata (~453-bit genomes) or recurrent neural nets (~448-bit); perfect scorers (89) appear within 100-200 generations and beat the hand-designed 81-point FSA, with FSAs consistently outperforming ANNs. repro=4 (real mutation/crossover/selection, below NEAT's 5 - fixed-length genomes, no complexification). open=2: one fixed fitness target. eco=0: a solo ant on a trail with no interaction (the sibling AntFarm system added pheromone communication and is deliberately NOT scored in this row). cog=3 (genuinely evolved controllers, no lifetime learning, matching Karl Sims/Framsticks). substrate=1 NOT 2: the FSA and ANN encodings are swappable alternatives run separately, which the MABE row already establishes scores as 1. morph=1 (grid, no physics), instr=2, vis=2. peer=4: a founding Artificial Life II paper whose trail task became a standard genetic-programming benchmark for decades. consc=0.

type: first digital-evolution experiment (1D numeric world on the IAS machine)
basis: VERIFIED real (Nils Aall Barricelli, von Neumann's IAS machine, Princeton 1953-1956; 'Numerical testing of evolution theories' Part I, Acta Biotheoretica 16(1/2):69-98, 1962, and Part II 16(3/4):99-126, 1963; source_url is Taylor, Dorin & Korb, 'Digital Genesis: Computers, Evolution and Artificial Life', arXiv:1512.02100, which documents the runs). Integers in a 1D array copy themselves under 'norms', with mutation norms, crossing between 'symbioorganisms', spontaneous formation, parasitism and symbiogenesis; later runs decoded genotypes into Tac Tix strategies and let winners reproduce. repro=4: genuine self-reproduction + mutation + competitive selection, below Tierra's 5 (tiny fixed rule space). open=3: his explicit 'unlimited evolution' goal (the term open-endedness later replaced) plus emergent parasites and symbiosis, but he reported runs homogenising - bounded novelty. eco=3 (parasite/symbiont interactions, matching Tierra). morph=1 (1D array, no physics). cog=1 (later game-playing genotypes are evolved strategies, no learning). instr=1 and vis=1: hand-analysed printouts, matching the Autopoietic Tessellation anchor. peer=4: the founding digital-evolution experiment, rediscovered by the Digital Genesis review. substrate=1, consc=0.

VERIFIED real (W. Grey Walter, Burden Neurological Institute; Elmer and Elsie built 1948-1949, shown to the press by December 1949, later units at the 1951 Festival of Britain, a second-generation unit at the Smithsonian; ROS and Nautilus histories corroborate). Two-vacuum-tube analogue 'brains', a rotating photocell, a contact switch and two motors give phototaxis, obstacle avoidance and battery-low homing to a recharging hutch; the CORA variant (Machina docilis) learned simple conditioned reflexes. repro=0/open=1: no reproduction or evolution of any kind. morph=3: real bodies in real physics, but one fixed hand-built body plan, below evolved or 3D-simulated bodies (GOLEM/Sims 5). cog=2 (reactive two-'neuron' control; CORA conditioning is a separate unit). eco=1 (two robots interacting through their head lamps, no resources). instr=1 (observation and long-exposure light-trail photographs). vis=2. peer=4: foundational for behaviour-based robotics and embodied A-Life. The mirror 'self-recognition' anecdote is NOT a consciousness mechanism: consc=0. substrate=1.

VERIFIED real (E. F. Codd, 'Cellular Automata', Academic Press 1968; LifeWiki OCA:Codd). Reduces von Neumann's 29-state universal constructor to 8 states on the von Neumann neighbourhood while keeping computation- and construction-universality; Codd showed a self-reproducing machine was possible but never gave a complete cell-by-cell design - one was built much later (LifeWiki gives the replicator as ~283 million cells; Devore's 1973 modification shrank it to ~95k). LINEAGE NOTE: same second-generation self-replication family as the von Neumann row, scored to mirror it (repro=4 tape-driven self-reproduction, open=2, instr=1, vis=2); peer=4 one step below von Neumann's founding 5. No ecology, physics, agents or learning (eco/morph/cog=0). substrate=1, consc=0.

VERIFIED real (Michael Conrad & Howard H. Pattee, 'Evolution experiments with an artificial ecosystem', Journal of Theoretical Biology 28:393-409, 1970; listed in the Pattee bibliography at the source_url and reviewed in Digital Genesis, arXiv:1512.02100). A materially closed artificial ecosystem in which organisms carry genetic material, reproduce with variation and compete; designed so mutualistic symbioses could arise. repro=4 (heredity + mutation + selection). open=2: Pachepsky et al. (Artificial Life 2002) report that attempts to evolve complex behaviour met limited success, and the authors themselves concluded variation and selection alone may not suffice. eco=3 (conserved resources, designed-for mutualism). morph=1, cog=1, instr=2, vis=1, peer=3 (J. Theor. Biol., niche adoption). Full text was not accessed - scores rest on the abstract-level record and two secondary reviews, so confidence is 0.7. substrate=1, consc=0.

VERIFIED real (Watson & Lovelock, 'Biological homeostasis of the global environment: the parable of Daisyworld', Tellus B 35B:284-289, 1983). type: evolutionary game-theory ecology with genome duplication
